text.tspan: Everyday English - B2 - 2026/09/15 - 01 - Essay
People share a meal and conversation.
Pexels · 9220890
Around the table
A good way to share a meal combines practical structure with an awareness of other people. Neither a rigid plan nor complete
improvisation is sufficient on its own; both need to be judged in context.
The practical case is straightforward: a simple plan leaves time for conversation. Consider how we prepare the vegetables before our
guests arrive. The benefit is not merely efficiency. A modest arrangement prevents avoidable confusion, leaving attention available
for the activity itself rather than for problems that could have been anticipated.
Consideration adds a second, equally important dimension: sharing the work helps everyone feel included. In this situation, each
guest brings one dish and helps clear the table. A decision can be convenient for one person while creating difficulty for another, so
its value depends partly on whose needs it recognises.
The most useful approach therefore brings structure and consideration together. Preparation establishes a workable starting point;
attention to other people keeps it responsive. Success should be assessed by how well the arrangement serves the experience,
rather than by how closely events follow the original plan.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example.
Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an
experience of your own.
Apply the idea to a real situation, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two
reasons are that a simple plan leaves time for conversation and that sharing the work helps everyone feel included. One example is
that we prepare the vegetables before our guests arrive.)
